title: 🌐 From embedded devices to NICs, switches and cloud systems
industry_title: Embedded systems, switching and cloud infrastructure

paras: The same functional building blocks appear at different scales, but architecture changes with power, latency, reliability and throughput needs.
Trackers, wearables, sensors and headphones: MCU/SoC, on-chip RAM/flash, radios, battery management and tight energy constraints.
Phones and laptops: CPU/SoC, DRAM, flash or SSD, GPU, wireless modem, display/audio controllers and OS services.
Smart intersections, cameras and vehicles: real-time constraints, rugged interfaces, accelerators, watchdogs and security/safety engineering.
Servers and accelerators: many cores, ECC DRAM, NVMe, high-speed NICs, redundancy, orchestration and observability.
Mainframes emphasize transaction integrity, virtualization and availability; supercomputers emphasize distributed numerical throughput. They are not the same architecture.

Ethernet: application → TCP/UDP/IP stack → NIC driver → NIC MAC → Ethernet PHY → copper/fiber medium → switch/router. MAC handles link framing; PHY handles physical signaling. The NIC may also offload checksum, segmentation, virtualization or cryptographic work.

Wireless: application → network stack → Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/cellular controller and baseband → RF transceiver/front end → antenna → air interface. Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and cellular are distinct protocol families with different link/control architectures.
Fiber: a transceiver module converts electrical signals to/from optical signals; switches and routers make forwarding decisions, not the optical module itself.

blocks.h2: Packet journey from physical port to a service
paras: NIC receives frame → DMA to memory → interrupt or polling/NAPI → kernel driver → Ethernet/IP processing → netfilter/routing → TCP/UDP socket → user-space server → response path. A virtual machine or container adds virtual NICs, bridges, veth pairs, namespaces, overlay encapsulation or virtual switches depending on deployment.

Hardware-to-organization connection: contracts define uptime and data protection expectations; engineers select NICs, topology, software and monitoring to meet those requirements. The business and technical layers are related, but a business department is not literally a VLAN.

blocks.h2: Compare an IoT sensor, laptop and cloud server
paras: For each system, identify: processing core(s), memory hierarchy, persistent storage, communication MAC/PHY/radio, power regulators, clock sources, operating environment, update mechanism, security boundary and service owner. Then trace one data item end to end and annotate every conversion, protocol and trust boundary.
